title: Three Weeks and One Short Form
subtitle: 数据统计 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 数据统计（人与社会·科学与技术·数据与统计）
meta: 主题语境：数据统计（人与社会·科学与技术·数据与统计）　|　核心词汇：input　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 input 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1998 the clerk ① checked the input that no colleague in the office would have recorded, and he said the checking was the whole of the week. The ② input, meaning the answer itself and not the form, ran three weeks and stayed unrecorded in the book; a input, he said, is the only thing in a office that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ input in that office had the same short form beside it, and the ④ input at the far screen, meaning the note they kept for the children to check and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A input, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the clerk said the recording is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the input was the whole of the matter, meaning the effort and not the answer. The ⑥ input, meaning the effort and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; input, he said, is either something you check or the only word that means both a answer and a effort. He said the effort is the part they remember.

By 2003 the ⑦ input had become a line in a sheet, and the sheet had become an argument about the short form. The ⑧ input of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three weeks of recording; input, he said, is either the note at the far screen or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ input I remember is the answer recorded in the sheet, which closed in 2005 and is still recorded as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ input, my mother said in 2007, is the only answer that improves by being recorded; every input, she said, is a effort that has agreed to look like a answer. She said the effort was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 投入；输入（指办公室里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 投入；输入（指那份填写内容本身，与表格相对）
C. 固定搭配：check the input 核对这份投入
D. n. 投入；输入（指留给孩子们核对的一条那一份）
E. n. 投入之事（抽象总称，指一处办公室的投入之事）
F. n. 投入；输入（指工作表里写到、被记下的的那一份）
G. n. 心力、贡献（指一件事里人人都填却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 贡献（抽象总称，指人人都填却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: checked the input that no colleague in the office would have recorded
The input, meaning the answer itself and not the form
the input at the far screen
the input was the whole of the matter
the input had become a line in a sheet
The input of the whole thing
A input, my mother said in 2007

answers.why: check the input 意为“核对这份投入”，1998 年那位办事员把办公室里没有一位同事肯记录的一份投入做了一遍。
input 意为“投入；输入”，指那份填写内容本身而不是表格，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记录。
input 意为“投入；输入”，指办公室里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一张薄薄的表格。
input 意为“投入；输入”，指最远那块屏幕旁留给孩子们核对的一条那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
input 意为“心力、贡献”，指一件事里人人都填却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份心力就是那件事的全部。
input 意为“贡献”，指人人都填却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份填写内容，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
input 意为“投入；输入”，指工作表里写到、被记下的的那一份，到 2003 年这一份成了工作表里的一行。
input 意为“投入之事”，办事员五月写道，整件事的投入之事是一处办公室和三个星期的记录。
input 意为“投入；输入”，我记得的是工作表里记录过的那一份，2005 年汇总了，至今仍被说成办公室里最安静的一份。
input 为抽象总称，母亲 2007 年说，投入是唯一会因为被好好记录而变得更好的填写内容。
